name: surfer
desc: Waveform viewer, supporting VCD, FST, or GHW format
why: A waveform viewer for VCD, FST, and GHW files that lets you watch digital circuits simulate and inspect their signals.

brief.what_it_is: Surfer is a waveform viewer for digital circuit simulation output. It reads VCD, FST, and GHW files (the docs also mention FTR, a memory transaction format) and lets you view and inspect the signals over time. It runs as a native desktop app on Linux, Windows, and macOS (ARM), and the homepage also links a browser version at app.surfer-project.org. It can also run headless as a server (surver) that a user connects to.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes Surfer as "An Extensible and Snappy Waveform Viewer". The user guide says it is built to be highly configurable.

commands_seen.context: Build and install Surfer from source via cargo; the docs describe this as the preferred install route. The docs say to replace surfer with surver to install the server-only version.
Install a specific tagged version (v0.4.0 is the example tag) into a chosen prefix. The docs say --locked matters so the exact dependencies from that release are used.
Start Surfer with no file loaded.
Start Surfer and load a waveform file directly. WAVEFORMFILE.vcd is a placeholder name in the docs.
Show the full list of command-line arguments and subcommands.
Subcommand from the usage text: starts Surfer in headless mode so a user can connect to it.

brief.install_notes: The homepage says building from source is the preferred route and should work on Linux, Mac, and Windows. Building from source needs a Rust compiler; the docs point to rust-lang.org/tools/install. Pre-built binaries are offered for Linux (x86, Rocky Linux x86, Linux ARM), Windows (x86), and macOS (ARM); the docs say the macOS binary is not signed, so most users cannot run it as is. Some Linux distributions package Surfer, and Homebrew has a formula. Compile-time features can be enabled or disabled. The docs do not describe any accounts, runtimes beyond Rust, or first-run configuration steps.
brief.standout: Surfer has a scripting-style command language (SUCL) that can run after a waveform loads, via -c/--command-file, --script, or -C/--command. The --script alias exists so VUnit can pass the same argument it uses with GTKWave. It can also run headless and accept a WCP connection (--wcp-initiate).
brief.status: Appears active but not confirmed. The GitLab project page shows a creation date of December 22, 2022, but I did not see a last-release or last-commit date. The docs refer to a v0.4.0 tag and to binaries built after each merge to main, and the homepage says development is ongoing at Linköping University. The docs also say Surfer versions are not yet that important.
brief.caveats: The docs say the GHW support is not as complete as VCD and FST. The browser version is slower than native and lacks some features, so the docs recommend installing the native build for day-to-day use. The macOS ARM binary is unsigned. Windows Defender has been known to flag Surfer as a trojan; the homepage suggests checking VirusTotal. The --command-file feature is described as temporary, to be removed once a proper scripting system exists. The license is EUPL-1.2. I did not find a dedicated README; the GitLab page loaded only project metadata.
